title: Evolvability and Selection: Is an Inherited Difference Selectable?
concept: Evolvability: whether a daughter-inherited chemical difference produces a REPRODUCIBLE, SELECTABLE fitness difference and the population shifts under selection rather than drifts — the Vasas-2010 evolvability null. Builds on the heritable difference transmitted by og-heredity (6A); this is the Gate-D selectable-fitness result.
gate_reason: Evolvability half of the former og-heredity (split from the inheritance half, og-heredity). Canonical arm og-34 (sharpened Gate D): a daughter-inherited chemical difference produces a reproducible, selectable fitness difference (parent-offspring correlation +0.949 vs a no-inheritance control; population shift +0.551 vs drift) against a matched no-inheritance null. Qualified. Carries plan_id 34 and the numeric handoff/builds_on edges to studies 35/36/37.
claim: A daughter-inherited chemical difference produces a reproducible, selectable fitness difference and the population shifts under selection rather than drifting: parent-offspring fitness correlation +0.949 vs a no-inheritance control, population shift +0.551 vs drift -0.004, against a matched no-inheritance null (og-34, canonical). Qualified — evolvability demonstrated on the modeled trait space; open-ended chemical novelty beyond that space is not.
question: Does a daughter-inherited chemical difference produce a reproducible, selectable fitness difference, and does the population shift under selection rather than drift?
hypothesis: An inherited compositional difference maps to a fitness difference that selection can act on, so the protocell lineage is evolvable, not merely heritable.
experiment: Run the sharpened Gate-D composite (og-34): measure parent-offspring fitness correlation and the population shift under selection against a matched no-inheritance null (daughters reset to a common composition), preserving the og-34 run provenance and findings.
result: Parent-offspring fitness correlation +0.949 vs a no-inheritance control and a population shift +0.551 vs drift -0.004 (perm p ~ 1e-4): the inherited difference is selectable and the population evolves. Qualified: shown on the modeled trait space; open-ended novelty is not.

findings.evidence_basis_note: The selectable-heredity signal over 8 seeds x 40 generations is the evolutionary model's outcome vs the vasas-2010 null.
findings.statement: There IS selectable chemical heredity (not the vasas-2010 null). Across 8 seeds x 40 generations at equal feeds, an inherited network-composition difference yields a reproducible parent-offspring fitness correlation (mean +0.949) far above the matched no-inheritance control (-0.018; permutation p=0.0001). Fitness is grounded in the real study-32/33 coupling (composition -> membrane retention -> standing pool -> division rate), so the correlation reflects a genuine mechanistic fitness consequence. Guardrail: selection acts on the inherited composition of the sustained A1 carbon-fixing network, not autocatalysis.

The inheriting population shifts composition measurably under selection (mean shift +0.551 toward higher-retention / longer-chain composition) while the matched no-inheritance control drifts (-0.004; permutation p=0.0002). Selection acts because both heritable variation and a reproducible fitness difference are present - the vasas-2010 evolvability caveat was tested (declared heritable variance sigma=0.03, not tuned) and the population shifts rather than drifts.

Heredity is carried by inherited NETWORK COMPOSITION (Option B, compositional / GARD-style), with the vasas-2010 evolvability caveat TESTED, not assumed - compositional inheritance carried enough selectable variance here for selection to act. Template copying (Option A, og-34a) is the higher-fidelity follow-on that would re-test selectable heredity under a copying mechanism, especially where compositional inheritance might prove too low-variance in other regimes.
